newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sasol sees similar second half profit.
newsitem.headline: Sasol sees similar second half profit.

text.p: South African synthetic fuel and chemical producer Sasol Ltd said on Tuesday it expected profit in the second half of its financial year to be similar to that of the first, barring major fluctuations in the rand and international prices.
Attributable income rose to 1,254 million rand from 1,025 million in the half year to December with the synthetic fuels division turning in a 25 percent increase in operating profit.

Sasol said the rise in synfuels earnings was "particularly pleasing" as it was achieved despite a significant drop in income resulting from the reduction in the floor price for purposes of calculating tariff protection to $18 a barrel.
Increases in international petroleum prices have resulted in zero tariff protection since November 1996.
Sasol said higher synfuel profits largely reflected continued stable plant conditions and a weaker rand, which averaged 4.51 against the dollar in the half year against 3.66 a year earlier.
Chemicals increased prices and volumes from existing and newly commissioned plants while higher oil division profits were helped by higher rand refining margins.
The mining business had a difficult time but Sasol said steps were being take to correct the situation and normal growth should be resumed during 1997/98.
Looking ahead, Sasol said the synfuel, chemicals and oil divisions were expected to continue to perform satisfactorily.
